clue.text: A way to protect one's castle to get stalemate game

definitions.text: A way to protect one's castle

parts.note: a stalemate in chess ends the game as a draw
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A chess player looks for a drawn result to keep their king safe.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess words 'castle' and 'stalemate' suggest a chess board, but the castle is a real fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised bridge over a moat kept attackers out of a medieval fortress.

clue.text: Show discharge when back is scratched

indicators.note: the back of the word is scratched off, so its final letter is removed

parts.note: demob is a release from military service

explanation.surface: An itchy rash oozes once someone scratches their back.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstration is a show, of a product or of public protest.

clue.text: When reckoning by English Duke is fictitious

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a sum is a calculation or reckoning

explanation.surface: An English duke's accounts are invented, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: An assumed name is a false one, adopted rather than real.

clue.text: Traumatised British Prime Minister mostly frightened to engage Republican

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the name is used

parts.note: Clement Attlee was the British Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951

indicators.note: to engage is to take in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: scared means frightened

explanation.surface: A post-war British leader, shaken and afraid, has to deal with a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was Labour Prime Minister after the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone marked by past conflict or hardship is described as damaged, figuratively, by old wounds.

clue.text: Mischievous child's play resulting in crash

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
an act is part of a play, or a performance

explanation.surface: A naughty child's game ends with something smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: A collision, the force of one thing striking another, is a crash.

clue.text: German found out, and complained

parts.note: rumbled is informal British for discovered or found out

explanation.surface: A German was caught out and protested about it.
explanation.walkthrough: To be rumbled, in British slang, is to have one's deception discovered.
explanation.definitionFit: To grumble is to mutter discontentedly, a mild form of complaining.

clue.text: Marx's lost love for music producer

indicators.note: lost means a letter is taken away from the name

parts.note: Harpo was one of the Marx Brothers
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A Marx brother mourns a lost sweetheart and a lost instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Harpo Marx famously played the instrument the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringed instrument is something that produces music.

clue.text: Nobel prize winner loses pound of gold

indicators.note: loses means a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a Nobel laureate is a prize winner
L is the abbreviation for pound (libra)

explanation.surface: A Nobel winner is a pound down from the gold medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aureate is a literary word for golden, from Latin aurum.

clue.text: Point of advert by Nationalist and Conservative

parts.note: a promo is a promotional advert
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the point is of an advert for two right-wing parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland jutting into the sea is called a point.

clue.text: Favourite pupil taken aback after teacher's blunder

indicators.note: after places the following piece behind the first

parts.note: Miss is the form of address for a female schoolteacher

indicators.note: taken aback means the word is written backwards

parts.note: a teacher's pet is a favourite pupil

explanation.surface: A teacher stuns the class pet with a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong step is figuratively an error or mistake.

clue.text: Bear park is halved, therefore

indicators.note: halved means only half of the word's letters are kept

parts.note: a ground is a sports field or park
ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: A wildlife park's bear enclosure gets cut in half, hence a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is halved' keeps the back half of GROUND, UND.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a hardship is to experience or endure it.

clue.text: Polluters stop getting smellier, oddly — no good in El Salvador

parts.note: an engine that dies stops running

indicators.note: oddly means the letters in odd positions are taken

parts.note: ES is the international vehicle registration code for El Salvador

explanation.surface: Factories that pollute stop causing such stinks in Central America.
explanation.definitionFit: Motors burning heavy fuel oil emit fumes, making them sources of pollution.

clue.text: I blame dodgy drinking spot not closing, and can't be appeased

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other
dodgy means unreliable, so the letters are put into a new order
not closing means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a place is a spot

explanation.surface: Someone blames a shady bar that won't close, and stays furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges I BLAME to IMABLE, which takes in PLAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone relentless, whose anger cannot be soothed, is unappeasable.

clue.text: Fuss as radioactive gas uncovered

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters are stripped away

parts.note: radon is a radioactive gas

explanation.surface: A panic as radioactive gas leaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: Much ado is commotion or bother, a synonym for fuss.

clue.text: Modern Christmas?

definitions.meaning: the festival when gifts are given, so a day of gifts

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading of a gift-giving day.
explanation.definitionFit: Contemporary means current; Christmas is jokingly the day for gifts.

clue.text: Root reckless at first, declaring; India will be put in

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: rash means reckless

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A rash declaration that India will be included sounds like a politician's root-and-branch plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent red vegetable eaten raw is a root crop.

clue.text: Always enthralled by cleavage, but is respectful

indicators.note: enthralled by means held inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a rent is a split or cleavage
ever means always

explanation.surface: A man always captivated by a low neckline still claims to be respectful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleavage' suggests a neckline; here it is a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A deeply respectful attitude shows reverence, as in worship.

clue.text: Hurriedly, Americans displaced by Europeans in London street

indicators.note: displaced by means one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: Pall Mall is a street in central London
the stretch holding both A's, each A standing for an American
the same stretch with each A swapped for E, the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Americans are hurriedly pushed out of a London street by Europeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Americans' is plural: both A's (A = American) become E's. Pall Mall is a London street of gentlemen's clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: In a disorderly rush is the adverbial sense of in a headlong hurry.

clue.text: Sailor from distant lands welcomed by prophet

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken in, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a seer is a prophet
afar means from a long way off

explanation.surface: A traveller from abroad is received by a holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: A seagoing traveller or mariner is a sailor.

clue.text: German in Britain is C of E, not Catholic

indicators.note: not means the letter is left out

parts.note: the Church of England is Anglican

explanation.surface: A German living in Britain belongs to the Church of England, not Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The Angles were a Germanic people who settled in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An Angle was one of the Germanic tribes that settled in early England.

clue.text: Inferior hellholes serve bottles

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, so the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: Second-rate dives serve drink in bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower in rank or quality, as in the minor of two, means inferior.

clue.text: Arrest 16 in Dieppe, including undertaker on vacation

indicators.note: including means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: seize is French for sixteen, and Dieppe is a French port; the 16 is a number, not a cross-reference

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied, so only the outer letters are kept

explanation.surface: An arrest in a French port involves an undertaker on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The '16' looks like a cross-reference to 16 Across but is French for sixteen. 'on vacation' leaves UR.
explanation.definitionFit: A seizure is a sudden fit or attack, as in cardiac arrest.

clue.text: Writer receives ten pence for film

indicators.note: receives means takes in, putting one piece inside

parts.note: a Bic is a ballpoint pen, a writer
10p, written as IOP

explanation.surface: A screenwriter is paid ten pence for a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 10P is read as the letters I, O, P.
explanation.definitionFit: A biographical movie about a real person is a type of film.

clue.text: Harridan's problem opening shed

indicators.note: the opening letter is shed, or cast off

parts.note: a snag is a problem

explanation.surface: A shrew has trouble getting the shed door open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden hut, but it is the verb, to cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: A scolding, nagging woman is a harridan, as is a shrew.

clue.text: Equipment belonging to baker trying to get a rise, but short of time, on peg

indicators.note: short of means the letter is missing

parts.note: trolling is deliberately provoking people online for a reaction
a pin is a peg

explanation.surface: A baker's kit tries to make dough rise but runs late on a hook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get a rise' suggests rising dough, but it means provoking a reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden cylinder for flattening pastry is a baker's tool.

clue.text: Unexpected photograph

explanation.definitionFit: A sudden decision is unplanned; a quick snapshot is a casual picture.

clue.text: Contract daughter to replace son in scam

indicators.note: to replace means one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: a swindle is a scam

explanation.surface: A deal brings in a daughter in place of a son as part of a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun, a deal, but it is the verb, to shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink or diminish gradually is to contract.

clue.text: Quietly engineer Unionist to join popular publishing house

parts.note: P is piano, quietly in music
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: An engineer quietly gets a Unionist to sign with a popular publisher.
explanation.definitionFit: Penguin Books is a well-known British publisher of paperbacks.

clue.text: American's vote against looking over conclusion to cyber-attack

indicators.note: over means the word is turned around

parts.note: nay is a vote against

indicators.note: conclusion to means the final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A US politician votes no after reviewing the end of a cyber attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Yank is informal slang for a person from the United States.

clue.text: Maverick to censor broadcast about dilapidated shack

indicators.note: about means going around the other piece

parts.note: to bleep is to censor swearing in a broadcast

indicators.note: dilapidated means falling apart, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A rebel censors a programme about a ruined hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dilapidated' is the anagram signal and 'about' puts the scrambled hut inside the censor's tone; 'broadcast' belongs to the bleep, not the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The odd one out of a family, a nonconformist, is a maverick.
